title: A failure is detected on the generic fibre
statement:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$0\leq q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \longleftarrow & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow f' & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

where $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K$, $S'$ is
an affine scheme, $K$ is a
field, $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is the displayed structural morphism, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ are the fibre-product projections, and $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf on
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ annihilated by $n$ such that

$$
f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F
$$

is not an isomorphism. If $S$ is separated, then moreover
$S'\to S$ is an affine morphism.
(*Stacks Project, [Tag `0F07`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F07).*)

proof.text: Negating universal degree-q base change supplies a preliminary base change S_1→S, a qcqs morphism g:T→S_1, and an n-torsion sheaf F whose degree-q map fails. The universal hypotheses in degrees 0,…,q−1 persist after this preliminary base change: each further base change is also a base change of f, by associativity of fibre products. Apply [sbc-lem-etale-locality], clause (3), with V_i the affine opens of S_1 and U_i=X_1×_{S_1}V_i. The U_i form an open, hence etale, cover of X_1; U_i→S_1 factors through V_i→S_1, which is open and hence etale. Its Cartesian diagrams are precisely the restrictions of the failing square, with F_i the inverse-image restriction of F to V_i×_{S_1}T. If every restricted map were an isomorphism the original map would be, so one affine open S' gives a failing square. Replace T by T×_{S_1}S' and write p:X'→S' for the resulting base change of f. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], clauses (3) and (2), g remains qcqs and T is a qcqs scheme. All later morphisms U→S' with U qcqs are qcqs by clause (1).

By [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity], clause (1), the failing map is injective, using the universal degree-(q−1) hypothesis. Exactness of geometric stalks makes every stalk map injective; conservativity implies that one stalk map is not bijective. Choose its geometric point x and ξ outside its image. Use [def-sbc-canonical-base-change-stalk-transitions] for the source stalk A(U), target stalk B(U), base-change map b_U and target restriction r_φ, with p:X'→S', Λ=Z/nZ and the fixed F. We may take the initial square to be the canonical pullback square, so its identity comparison is the identity. Define P(U→T) by t_U(ξ)∉im(b_U). Thus P(T) holds. The comparison maps are linear and preserve the coefficient n-torsion condition. The passage to module coefficients uses [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] with Λ=Z/nZ and with the vertical and horizontal sides exchanged. An abelian sheaf killed by n has the unique Λ-action [a]z=az; conversely every Λ-module sheaf is killed by n. Clauses (1)–(3) identify the inverse images, derived direct images and actual base-change arrow after forgetting Λ, and exactness identifies their degree-q cohomology. Thus failure of the abelian map is failure of the module map. Choose ξ in this identified module target stalk and carry out the transition, limit and coefficient arguments in that module category throughout. Whenever the abelian injectivity and stalk lemmas are applied, apply them to the forgotten module square and use these canonical comparisons; kernels, cokernels and stalk elements retain their underlying abelian groups. At the final field square the same comparison identifies the failed module map with the abelian map in the conclusion. This uses a derived coefficient-comparison theorem, not merely the equivalence of the n-torsion sheaf categories.

For a thickening i:U→V over T, [lem-sbc-source-transition-thickening] and [lem-sbc-target-transition-thickening] give isomorphisms on the source and target stalks, respectively; the target fibre square is Cartesian by its construction. Here is the compatibility calculation r_i b_V=b_U s. Work first with derived functors, writing u^* and Ru_* and suppressing the canonical composition isomorphisms; take degree-q cohomology and the fixed stalk afterwards. Write g_V:V→S', a:X'×_{S'}U→X'×_{S'}V, and F_V for the coefficient on V. The transitions are the adjunction-unit transitions of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions]. Under the adjunction for h_U, and the identification h_U^*p^*=e_U^*i^*g_V^*, the transpose of r_i b_V is e_U^*i^*ε_{g_V}(F_V). The transpose of b_U s is e_U^* of the composite ε_i(i^*F_V) ∘ i^*ε_{g_V}(Ri_*i^*F_V) ∘ i^*g_V^*Rg_{V,*}(η_i(F_V)). Naturality of ε_{g_V} rewrites its last two factors as i^*η_i(F_V) ∘ i^*ε_{g_V}(F_V). The triangular identity ε_i(i^*F_V) ∘ i^*η_i(F_V)=1 therefore gives the same transpose. These are precisely the mate and transition formulas in the two cited definitions, so equality of transposes proves the required equality; the canonical coefficient composition maps identify F_U with i^*F_V. Consequently r_i sends im(b_V) onto im(b_U), since s is surjective, and reflects membership, since r_i is injective. By [lem-sbc-stalk-transport-composition], r_i(t_V ξ)=t_U ξ. Hence P(U) iff P(V). This verifies thickening invariance without treating an equivalence of sites as an equality of categories.

Let D be a small cofiltered inverse system of qcqs T-schemes with affine transitions, with limit cone c, and suppose P(D_i) for every i. If t_c ξ=b_c η for some η∈A(c), [lem-sbc-source-image-limit-descent] supplies i and η_i with r_{c_i}(b_i η_i)=b_c η. By [lem-sbc-stalk-transport-composition], the element δ=b_i η_i−t_i ξ restricts to zero at c. Apply [lem-sbc-target-limit-zero-detection] to δ: some arrow j→i makes r_{ji}(δ)=0. Then t_j ξ=r_{ji}(b_i η_i), which belongs to im(b_j) by [lem-sbc-target-stalk-restriction-image]. This contradicts P(D_j). Thus P(c). All limit lemmas require S' affine, small cofiltered indexing, qcqs stages and affine transitions, precisely the assumptions here. In the directed-set version of the minimal-counterexample lemma the index category is small and cofiltered as required.

For U→T qcqs and a closed immersion i:Z→U with quasi-compact open complement j:V→U, suppose both P(Z) and P(V) fail. Put ζ=t_U ξ. Transport composition gives r_i ζ∈im(b_Z) and r_j ζ∈im(b_V). Apply [lem-sbc-closed-open-coefficient-embedding] to F_U: there is a monomorphism F_U→G=j_*J⊕i_*i^*F_U, where J is the chosen injective Z/nZ-module sheaf containing j^*F_U. By [lem-sbc-open-injective-coefficient-zero], the open coefficient image of ζ is zero. Its hypotheses hold: S' is affine, q≥1, U is qcqs, V is quasi-compact and p has universal base change in every nonnegative degree less than q. The negative-degree maps, if the integer indexing convention is used, are automatically maps between zero higher images. By [lem-sbc-closed-coefficient-range], the closed coefficient image of ζ lies in the closed-summand base-change image. These are exactly the two implications in the cited statements; no exactness of j_* is asserted.

The two summand components reconstruct the coefficient image of ζ in the cokernel for G: the open component is zero and the closed component is in the image, so that cokernel class is zero. The finite direct sum decomposition is preserved by inverse image, derived direct image and stalks: each additive functor sends the equations π_aι_b=δ_ab and ι_1π_1+ι_2π_2=1 to the same equations. Naturality of the base-change mate in the coefficient sheaf identifies the component base-change maps. Clause (2) of [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity], applied to the coefficient monomorphism F_U→G and the qcqs map U→S', injects the original cokernel into this cokernel. Exactness of geometric stalks preserves that injection and computes the stalk cokernel. Therefore ζ∈im(b_U), contrary to P(U). This proves P(U)⇒P(V) or P(Z), the closed–open condition.

For U=∅ the fibre X'×_{S'}U is empty. On the small etale site of ∅ every object is empty and its empty covering forces sections of any abelian sheaf to be the zero group. Thus the only coefficient sheaf is zero, every complex on this site is zero, and its higher direct images are zero. Hence B(∅)=0, t_∅ ξ=0=b_∅(0), and P(∅) fails. Apply [sbc-lem-bc-minimal-counterexample] with the four conditions proved above and P(T): it gives a field K and Spec K→T with P(Spec K). The coefficient is the pullback of F, still annihilated by n; non-membership in the stalk image prevents the field-square map from being an isomorphism. Pasting its pullback square with X'→S'→S gives the required diagram.

If S is separated its diagonal S→S×_{Spec Z}S is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For an affine open W=Spec B⊂S write S'=Spec A. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies S'×_S W→S'×_{Spec Z}W with the pullback of that diagonal along the pair of structural maps to S. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] this pullback is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with R=Z, its target is Spec(A⊗_Z B). The affine-chart characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore identifies S'×_S W with Spec((A⊗_Z B)/I) for an ideal I. Every inverse image of an affine open W is thus affine, so [pqf-def-affine-morphism] gives that S'→S is affine.
